what: Grade of the 13 rule-4 edges that became reachable when tier 3 made partial paths resolvable. Rule 4's 0.970 was measured at 420147b on the spans reachable under the OLD resolver; these 13 arrived under the new one and that number never covered them.
how_to_grade: For each entry read `source_text` and decide whether it refers to `target_label` at `target_file`.
These are the PARTIAL-PATH-scoped subset: the line names a path that is a suffix of the target,
not the full repo path. Identified by property, not by the author’s say-so: of 32 path-scoped
edges, 19 carry the full path on the line and 13 do not. 19 + 13 = 32.

pins.population_stable: 32 path-scoped / 19 exact / 13 partial — identical across two forced rebuilds

method: FULL POPULATION, all 13, graded from the document prose. The grader wrote neither the rule nor the resolver.
caveat: n=13. One correct population is not a precision floor for the rule as a whole; rule 4 now has 33 edges graded across two commits by one outside party (32 at 420147b, these 13 at b8dfc25), not a single measurement.
note_refuted: One suspicion raised and refuted during grading: `getChangedFiles` and `getChangedFilesSync` both resolve to freshness/git.js from the same line, which looked like a substring match. A standalone-token test showed both appear as independent tokens. Not a word-boundary defect.
